item.description: With butter prices slipping through our fingers, we took matters into our own hands. Summer read – originally published May 28 2025. Every day it feels like there’s a new headline about Aotearoa’s butter price blowout. With Stats NZ reporting a 65% price hike since February last year, a block of butter is slipping out of reach for many, with the rise unlikely to melt away anytime soon. item.description: Alex Casey goes in search of ‘Crawl’ by Atlas, the beloved mid-2000s emo anthem that’s ‘fallen between the cracks’. Summer read – originally published August 18 2025. It’s some time in 2007 and Britomart is swarming with gloomy loiterers, their sullen faces hidden behind swooping side fringes, black eyeliner and snakebite piercings. item.title: Inside the dying industry of cargo ship travel
item.description: Until 2020, it was possible to book a voyage on a cargo ship. Today, it’s virtually impossible, despite being a greener, languid alternative to air travel. Summer read – originally published March 26 2025. Before the time of te Tiriti, there were few passenger ships. Crossing the Pacific in 1830? Usually, only a merchant could take you – and if you didn’t want to be swindled, swabbing decks, or marooned as a stowaway, you needed to hire a middleman like Hamish Jamieson. item.description: Books editor Claire Mabey unravels the dark questions at the heart of the latest book by one of Aotearoa’s most prolific and successful novelists. item.description: This under-seen follow-up to New Zealand Today is a high point in Guy Williams’ career, writes Tom Augustine. Summer read – originally published October 15 2025.
